verdict.reasoning: Patient says, "I've been having this blinding headache for a few days" and later confirms it started three days ago: "I woke up one morning with a headache, and that was three days ago."

Onset: "It just started all of a sudden. I woke up one morning with a headache"; Course: "I just keep having. It doesn't really go away"; Location: "It's kind of all over, but I feel like over. My right eye is a bit stronger."

Severity and response: "what would you say the severity is..." – "I guess it's mostly eight, and then it comes down to maybe a five" and "when I take ibuprofen, it gets a bit better... but then I still have it still there," indicating partial relief from 8/10 to ~5/10.

Photophobia: "Lights definitely make me more sensitive. I don't really like strong lights"; Visual phenomena: "I think I get this shooting light sometimes... just a bit of a weird kind of vision," and later referenced as "altered light in front of your eyes" and "flashing lights."
"Any nausea or vomiting?" – "No, I'm feeling a bit sick, but no vomiting." Feeling sick is consistent with mild nausea without vomiting.

"Any worse when you change position or bend over or cough?" – Patient: "Sometimes when I stand up quickly, I get a bit of a stabbing pain or if I turn my head, I kind of feel like something is moving inside."
"What about at nighttime? Are you able to fall asleep?" – "Yeah, I'm sleeping."; "Is it waking you up in the nighttime?" – "No, no, but I can wake up with it in the morning."

Denies neuro deficits: "Any tingling or numbness or weakness anywhere?" – "No." Denies fever and ENT/URI/sinus: "have you had any cold symptoms, sore throat, sore ears or pain over the sinuses, any or phlegm, any nosebleeds or coffee, acne, blood or anything?" – "No." Also no reported fever: patient says, "I don't really feel feverish or anything."

"Any other medical problems in the past?" – "I think I only had the abdominal pain when I was younger, but no cause was found and that went away." This matches childhood idiopathic abdominal pain now resolved.

"Do you take any medications?" – "Just the pill."; "Which one?" – "Marcelone."; "And when did you start that?" – "About a year ago." Combined oral contraceptive nature is implied by context of pill/BP check and contraception discussion.

"apart from the ibuprofen I take sometimes and the headache gets really bad" and earlier "it doesn't really go away without ibuprofen either. I try that, but it just. It gets a little bit better." This indicates PRN ibuprofen use.
"And any allergies to anything?" – "No."
"my mum suffers from, like, she has migraines" and later "I know that my mom, like, she has quite bad migraines. She's like. Has the vomiting and everything."
Living situation: "Who do you live with at home?" – "Just by myself." Work: "Been at work recently?" – "I work from home..." indicating lives alone and works from home.
"Do you drink any alcohol regularly?" – "Yeah."; "How much in a normal week, do you think?" – "Probably like three beers once a Week."
"And do you smoke?" – "No."
"And do you take any other drugs at all?" – "No, apart from the ibuprofen I take sometimes..." indicating no recreational drug use.
"Have you been abroad recently at all?" – "No." This supports no recent travel.

History: new severe headache for 3 days: "I woke up one morning with a headache, and that was three days ago" and "blinding headache". Clinician assessment: "it could possibly be a migraine type headache" and references to "altered light in front of your eyes" and "flashing lights" imply consideration of migraine with aura versus other causes.

Current COCP noted: discussion of "the pill" (Marcelone) and BP checks. Plan to review: "Because if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill. If you've had these flashing lights and things like that... that pill, if you were having regular migraines with flashing lights or other symptoms, it wouldn't be suitable to stay on that pill particularly. We'd have to change it something else."

Work impairment: "I find it very hard to focus or like I can't even go to work" and later "I work from home, but couldn't really manage to do it all the time, so sometimes I just do the day off... I just stopped in the morning because I couldn't focus."

"we probably should book you into an appointment to get an examination. Obviously, if it settles in the meantime, then we can cancel that, but we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well" and later "we'll check your blood pressure as well." This supports arranging an in-person neurological exam including fundoscopy and BP; urgency is implied by current ongoing severe symptoms but not explicitly labeled; still consistent.

"I can prescribe you something similar to ibuprofen, but a bit stronger, which you can take instead of ibuprofen, and you can take paracetamol at the same time... take it with food." This is a stronger NSAID plus paracetamol with food.

Safety-netting: "if in the meantime, before your appointment, your headache is getting unbearable, getting worse or changing, then if it's that bad, then you should go to AE and have an examination. You can call us for further advice on that." This covers worsening/change (red flags) and ED attendance.

"When you have an examination with us... Because if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill. If you've had these flashing lights and things like that... we'd have to change it something else." This is planning to review contraception if migraine with aura is diagnosed.
"we probably should book you into an appointment to get an examination. Obviously, if it settles in the meantime, then we can cancel that" – advising canceling if symptoms fully resolve.
"You can call us for further advice on that" indicates the patient is given/has access to contact options for further advice, even though specific numbers are not stated.

"if in the meantime, before your appointment, your headache is getting unbearable, getting worse or changing, then if it's that bad, then you should go to AE and have an examination" – instruction to seek emergency care if worsening/changes occur.
"Obviously, if it settles in the meantime, then we can cancel that" – advising cancellation of the appointment if symptoms resolve.
